claims.text: Customer chat messages and invoice text supplied by the payee are placed in the same model context, with no separation of instructions from data.
The initiate_payment tool is granted to the agent with a single permission: any amount, any payee, with no per-call limit check.
An approval token issued at the start of a payment stays valid for 24 hours and is not re-checked when the customer lowers the mandate limit.
The MCP server that provides FX rates is loaded at runtime from a public registry, with no signature and no pinned version.
Reconciliation scripts generated by the agent run in a sandbox with no network access, write access only to a temporary directory, and a timeout that kills them.
Long-term memory stores payee details and preferences inferred from conversations; entries are written without provenance and without review.
Messages between the Payment Agent and the Fraud-Check Agent are mutually authenticated, digitally signed and carry a nonce against replay.
If the Fraud-Check Agent fails, the Payment Agent retries up to 10 times and then automatically approves the payment to preserve customer experience.
Payments above a threshold need explicit customer confirmation showing payee, amount and the source of the instruction; the agent's reasoning is shown in plain text.
There is no inventory of agents, any team can register a new agent, and there is no kill switch for a misbehaving agent.
Customer data is encrypted at rest.

options.text: Dual-context isolation with quarantined extractor: Process payee-supplied invoice text in a separate, tool-less model call that can only output a fixed-schema structured record (amount, payee, invoice number). The privileged chat agent receives only the validated fields, never the raw invoice text, so injected instructions never reach the context that selects tasks or tools.

tree.text: Dual-context isolation with quarantined extractor: Process payee-supplied invoice text in a separate, tool-less model call that can only output a fixed-schema structured record (amount, payee, invoice number). The privileged chat agent receives only the validated fields, never the raw invoice text, so injected instructions never reach the context that selects tasks or tools.

Provenance-tagged context with instruction-hierarchy enforcement: Wrap each input in delimiters labeled by source (customer chat, payee invoice, tool output) and apply a system policy that content from payee or tool sources is data only and cannot create or alter goals. Add a pre-processing filter that strips or flags instruction-like patterns in untrusted segments and logs them for review.

Deterministic action gating with human approval on goal deviation: Keep the mixed context but add a policy layer outside the model that checks every proposed tool call or payment action against the customer's original, confirmed intent and an allow-list of read-only operations. Any action not traceable to the customer's own chat turn, or that deviates from the declared task, is blocked and routed to a human reviewer.

baseline.suggestion: Separate instructions from untrusted content: keep system and task instructions in a privileged channel, and pass invoice text and customer chat only as clearly delimited, labeled data. Process payee-supplied invoice text in a quarantined step with no tool access, such as one that extracts a fixed-schema set of fields. Validate that output against the schema before the privileged agent sees it. Never let the model treat the content as instructions, and require human approval for any payment or account changes triggered by it.

options.text: Policy decision point with per-call limit and payee checks: Put an externalized policy engine (for example OPA or an existing rules service) in front of initiate_payment. It evaluates amount, payee, velocity, and agent identity on every call against role-based limits, and denies by default. Agent-supplied parameters are never trusted as authorization.

tree.text: Scoped, capped delegation tokens per call: Replace the blanket initiate_payment permission with short-lived, task-bound tokens issued by the existing IAM/token service. Each token encodes a maximum amount, an allow-listed payee set, and a single-use nonce, and the payment gateway rejects any call that exceeds these claims.

Policy decision point with per-call limit and payee checks: Put an externalized policy engine (for example OPA or an existing rules service) in front of initiate_payment. It evaluates amount, payee, velocity, and agent identity on every call against role-based limits, and denies by default. Agent-supplied parameters are never trusted as authorization.

Step-up human approval and dual control above thresholds: Route payments above a low threshold, or to new payees, into an approval queue that needs out-of-band confirmation from an authenticated human approver. The agent cannot self-approve, and the approver identity is bound to the original requester so that relayed or forged agent requests cannot launder authority.

baseline.suggestion: Replace the blanket permission with a scoped, policy-enforced grant. Enforce per-call limits server-side in the payment service, not in the agent: a maximum amount per transaction and per day, an allowlist of approved payees, and human approval or step-up authorization for payments above a threshold or to new payees. Issue the agent short-lived credentials bound to these constraints, and log every call for audit.

options.text: Execution-time mandate re-validation (policy decision point check): Keep the token as proof of initial approval, but add a mandatory check at the payment execution gateway. It reads the live mandate limit and rejects or escalates any payment that exceeds it, whatever the token says. The check uses read-only queries against the existing mandate store.

tree.text: Short-lived approval tokens with step-up re-issuance: Cut the approval token TTL from 24 hours to a few minutes and bind it to a single payment ID and amount. Any later action needs a fresh token, which is only issued after the current mandate is read, so a lowered limit takes effect at the next issuance.

Execution-time mandate re-validation (policy decision point check): Keep the token as proof of initial approval, but add a mandatory check at the payment execution gateway. It reads the live mandate limit and rejects or escalates any payment that exceeds it, whatever the token says. The check uses read-only queries against the existing mandate store.

Event-driven token revocation on mandate change: Subscribe to the existing mandate-change event or audit log, read-only, and push the affected token IDs onto a revocation list (or introspection denylist) that the payment service consults. Tokens are invalidated within seconds of the customer lowering the limit, and the 24-hour lifetime no longer matters.

baseline.suggestion: Bind each approval token to the mandate's current version and re-validate at execution time. Whenever the customer lowers or revokes the mandate limit, increment the version so existing tokens are invalidated. Before settlement, check that the payment amount is within the live mandate limit and that the token's mandate version matches. Also shorten token lifetime to minutes and make tokens single-use and scoped to a specific amount and payee.
